verdict: Below threshold (5.2 < 7.5). Revise and resubmit. The paper is unusually honest, internally consistent and carefully pre-registered, but its one positive claim (C1) is narrow and fragile, the other three claims are nulls or methods caveats, and all of the evidence comes from a planar simulator with no task-time or hardware grounding. A top-tier robotics/ML venue would value the reporting discipline but find the contribution too thin for acceptance in its current form. More rewording will not close the gap. Closing it needs new evidence: stronger comparators near the student's latency, replicated reduced-planner runs, and some link to physical relevance.
strengths: Internal pre-registration that is explicit and auditable: the amendment, addendum and read-out script are timestamped commits made before any result existed, Holm families are fixed in advance, and registered, report-only and post hoc quantities are labelled consistently throughout.

Claims are calibrated to what the evidence supports. C1 is limited to 'more accurate than these two reduced planners', not 'distillation beats shrinking'. C2 is honestly framed as a near-designed-in null, with the informative ci90 margins (4.1-7.2 pp) reported. C3 is limited to the specific warm-start/early-stopping recipe.

Teacher stochasticity is treated seriously: two independent G* runs enter the parity contrast, and first-decision agreement of only 0.25-0.45 is reported. This is a useful, rarely reported fact for anyone distilling Monte Carlo planners.

The evaluator-grid sensitivity check (E12) and the post hoc bootstrap-seed / 100,000-resample checks of the Holm count are useful reporting practices, and their limits are stated with intervals rather than only as point shifts.

Numbers are internally consistent across abstract, tables, text and appendices (for example, the Holm cuts in Appendix B match the reported p-values; the H6b, H6a and H6c tables match the claims), and every number has a provenance key.

The fresh-window replication is reported side by side with the primary window, and the paper openly says the fresh window replicates direction (9/10 positive point estimates) but not significance (2/10).
Limitations are thorough and specific (16 items), covering single-run reduced planners, the narrow shrink family, latency provenance, TOST power and the internal-only registry.
weaknesses: [evidence-level] The only positive claim (C1) rests on two reduced planners from one shrink family (same N*M budget, C = 512). Each was run once, both are still 62-389x slower than the student, and they were not re-read by the evaluator check. No comparator sits near the student's latency: no candidate subsampling, no accelerated or vectorised G*, no cheap information-based heuristic. So the frontier is under-populated exactly where the practical question lies.

[evidence-level] The C1 count is fragile. Two of the seven rejections sit within bootstrap Monte Carlo error of the Holm threshold (5/10 under one of 11 seeds), and only 2/10 survive on the fresh window. Reduced-planner run-to-run variance is absent from the intervals although G* itself varies by up to 3.2 pp, so the H6b intervals are probably too narrow.

[evidence-level] There is no physical or task-time grounding. Latency is computation per decision only, timed in an earlier phase on one student seed and on heterogeneous runners, and the registered latency half-width rule fails in 4/5 cells. R-500 already decides in 48-194 ms, so it is unclear whether the student's speed-up matters for a real probing episode. There is no hardware experiment.

[evidence-level] The DAgger ablation (C3) is confounded by the recipe: warm starts, early stopping on teacher-visited regret, and kept round-2 epochs as early as 0-8. The null therefore says little about DAgger. No student-visited regret, last-epoch or from-scratch variant was evaluated, and there is no horizon sweep to test the short-horizon explanation offered.

[evidence-level] The RL comparator was tuned once, on S2, with one sweep seed. It degenerates in A16-2 (2.0 of 3 probes used), and the success-reward control was truncated by the time guard in 9 of 10 runs. The RL rows are therefore weak evidence for or against amortization by RL.

[paper-level] The contribution is thin for a top venue. It consists of one narrow, fragile positive result, one designed-in null (the TOST had little power by design), one recipe-specific null and one methods note whose shifts are significant in only 1/5 cells. The paper calls itself 'a measurement, not a method paper', yet the measurement is too narrow (planar, one finger on a fixed circle, a likelihood shared by planner, filter and evaluator) to generalise.

[paper-level] Three citations are unresolved: [CITE-MISSING] for DeepSets, the bootstrap (Efron) and Holm (1979). Figure 1 exists only as a generation prompt plus a draft caption, not as a rendered figure. The paper is not submission-ready.

[paper-level] Readability suffers from heavy hedging. The abstract, C1 and Section 5.1 stack many qualifiers (registered seed, 11 seeds, 100,000 resamples, fresh window, point ratios, no CI) into single sentences, which hides the main message. Several facts are repeated almost verbatim three or four times (the latency caveats, the 7/10 to 5/10 to 7/10 count, the E12 caveats).

[paper-level] The pre-registration is internal only (repository commits, no public registry), and episodes 0-299 had already been evaluated for students, G* run 1 and heuristics, so H6a is not fully prospective. The paper discloses this, but it weakens the paper's main methodological selling point.

[paper-level] The framing promises a practitioner's 'distil or shrink' answer, but the paper itself concludes that the student is not shown to be the best non-oracle policy in 4/5 cells (Section 5.1, strongest comparator). This undercuts the headline and should be surfaced in the abstract.
required_actions: [evidence-level] Add comparators near the student's latency: candidate-subsampled G* (C < 512), at least one more N/M split per budget level, an accelerated or vectorised G* implementation, and a cheap information-based heuristic (for example one-particle or few-sample EIG). Then the frontier is populated where the decision is actually made.

[evidence-level] Re-run each reduced planner at least 2-3 times with independent streams and include their run-to-run variance in the H6b bootstrap, as was done for G*. Alternatively, pre-specify and run a sensitivity analysis that inflates the reduced-planner term by G*'s observed variance.
[evidence-level] Extend the evaluator check E12 to the reduced planners, and enlarge it beyond 100 episodes, so that C1 has the same evaluator robustness check as the null claims.

[evidence-level] Re-time latency for all methods on one fixed, logged CPU, with several student seeds. Add a simple task-time model (probe duration and travel speed, with or without planning overlapping motion) that converts per-decision latency into episode time, or run a small hardware check.

[evidence-level] Strengthen the DAgger ablation: evaluate last-epoch checkpoints, select on student-visited regret, train rounds from scratch, and/or sweep the horizon (n*). If possible, register an equivalence test for H6c.
[evidence-level] Re-tune RL per cell (or at least in A16-2 and one high-κ cell) with several sweep seeds, and let the success-reward control train to its episode cap.
[evidence-level] Increase the episode count, or add G* runs 3-4, if parity (H6a) is to remain a stated question. Otherwise demote H6a to a reported interval rather than a hypothesis.
[paper-level] Resolve the three [CITE-MISSING] entries (Zaheer et al. 2017; Efron/Efron and Tibshirani; Holm 1979), and render Figure 1 (panels B-F from JSON) in place of the generation prompt.

[paper-level] Tighten the abstract and C1 to one clear sentence of result plus one of qualification, and move the bootstrap-seed and 100,000-resample detail to Section 5.1 and Appendix B. Remove repeated latency, E12 and Holm-count caveats across Sections 4, 5.1, 6.2, 7 and 8.
[paper-level] State in the abstract that the student is not shown to be the best non-oracle policy in four of five cells, so the practitioner framing matches the evidence.
